YOUR UNIT, verbatim:
### U9b1e — The broker closes its ledger when its harness ends it by signal

The controller ran its real-harness check on U9b1d's tree (2026-11-01, 2b96d97bb, Claude Code 2.1.316, haiku, the scratch realm of U9b1d's check, its dialect binding no secret). U9b1d holds: Claude Code's MCP log shows `Calling MCP tool: resolve` on `cap-library-docs` and `Tool 'resolve' completed successfully`, the seat wrote its result ("received documentation ID nnp-check-7Qx"), the journal shows `capability-call-settled` `succeeded` with the response's digest, and the response is retained. The same holds with the seat also granted the native `web-search` beside the brokered grant (WebSearch reached the seat; no `Unexpanded`). Every such run then parked: "effect … failed 1 of 1 attempt(s); last error: broker ledger lifecycle is invalid". Claude Code's MCP log for both servers ends "Sending SIGINT to MCP server process". `brokkr hands serve` handles a termination signal (`exit.rs`); `brokkr broker serve` (`crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker.rs`) installs no handler, so the signal kills it before it writes Closed, and CR3 refuses a ledger with no Closed after the process settles. The deterministic fixture harness ends a session by closing the broker's standard input, so no suite could see this.

The change: an interrupt or termination signal (SIGINT, SIGTERM) that reaches `brokkr broker serve` is its harness ending the session, as a closed standard input is. The broker reads no new frame after it; a call already accepted ends as CR3 and CR4 say for a session that ends (its Terminal if the server's answer arrives within the existing bounds, the existing local ending otherwise); the server box is settled as the existing ending settles it; Closed is written and fsynced, Clean unless a fatal cause latched first, which the signal never overwrites; and the broker exits as a normal session end. A signal before the session is served (during admission or box establishment) ends it with the existing cause for that stage, and records nothing the stage did not. A second signal, or the existing deadlines, still bound how long it waits. The check of a ledger is unchanged: a ledger without Closed still refuses "broker ledger lifecycle is invalid". `brokkr hands serve` and its signal handling are unchanged.

Files: `crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker.rs`, `crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker/session.rs` and `crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker/rpc.rs`; by ruling R6, `crates/brokkr-cli/Cargo.toml` for one dependency edge and its one `Cargo.lock` line; with new private children as the standing child-module rule allows, and their tests; the enabled suite's fixture harness (a mode that ends a served session by SIGINT, as Claude Code 2.1.316 does, and one by SIGTERM) and a new child module of `crates/brokkr-cli/tests/capability_broker/enabled.rs`. No public item added or changed. No edit to `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs` (another lane holds it), `adapters/*.json`, `adapters/mcp/admit.rs` or the ledger's record grammar (`crates/brokkr-protocol/src/broker/ledger.rs`). If the change cannot be made without one of those, stop and report it.

Closes tasks 46.8 and 46.9; requirements [CR3](specs/capability-response-retention/spec.md), [CR4](specs/capability-response-retention/spec.md), [MB1](specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md).
Proof: through the real binary, a seat holding one brokered grant, whose harness ends the session by SIGINT after its call is answered, completes with the call settled `succeeded`, its response retained and the ledger Closed Clean; the same by SIGTERM; a harness that signals while a call is in flight leaves that call ended as CR3 and CR4 say and the ledger Closed; a signal during admission ends with that stage's existing cause. Independent compiling removals of the signal handling and of its closure each fail their own test. Host evidence, the controller's: the real Claude check on this tree completes, and the call and its retained response are read back through `inspect`.

Controller ruling R5 2026-11-01 (under the operator's standing ruling of 2026-10-28, the recommended option of the controller's real-harness check finding on U9b1d's tree; the alternatives were a wrapper that turns the harness's signal into a closed standard input, which adds a process to every brokered launch, and accepting an unclosed ledger when the harness exited 0, which would break CR3 and is refused): this small unit lands after U9b1d and before U9b2, whose guides then describe a grant a real Claude seat can complete; any other file comes back to the operator. The house MCP grant waits for this unit as well.

Controller ruling R6 2026-11-01 (under the operator's standing ruling of 2026-10-28, the recommended option (a) of run 1's finding): run 1 built R5 and proved it on the host through the real binary, including the controller's failure reproduced by a removal of the handler, but needed one file outside the row. Neither std nor the CLI's rustix features install a signal handler; rustix's runtime module is Linux-only, and decision 0063 needs macOS too; and brokkr-protocol re-exports no signal API. So the row gains `crates/brokkr-cli/Cargo.toml` for one dependency edge, `signal-hook = "0.3.18"`, under `[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]`, the version brokkr-protocol already holds, and its one `Cargo.lock` line. No registry version moves and no new crate enters the lockfile. The handlers only write signal-hook's self-pipe, and the session drains it on its own threads, so no handler writes the ledger. Option (b), libc with an unsafe `sigaction` and a hand-written self-pipe, adds unsafe code for what the held crate does. Option (c), a brokkr-protocol re-export, is public API growth outside the row. Both are refused. Run 1's commit is replayed into run 2 uncommitted.

Owning tests: the tests beside `crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker.rs` and its children, and `crates/brokkr-cli/tests/capability_broker/enabled.rs` and its child modules.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],

    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},

    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},

  ],
```

members.correctness: Correctness/fit review of 1aff3d020 (U9b1e) against 2fe8308d2. VERDICT: the change does what R5/R6 frame, inside the row (broker.rs, session/lifetime.rs, rpc.rs, existing private child rpc/calls.rs, Cargo.toml one cfg(unix) edge signal-hook 0.3.18, one Cargo.lock dependency line, no new crate). No public item, no edit to adapters.rs, adapters/*.json, admit.rs, ledger.rs, exit.rs or hands serve. CHECKED: `git diff e31bf8ec2 HEAD -- crates/ Cargo.lock` is empty, so the production code is the code the controller host-checked. Design read: startup cancels on 1 signal (orphaned|at_least(1)), so each stage keeps its own cause. Serving takes the 1st signal as hang-up (asked returns Ok(None) with no active call, so the existing hung_up() ends Ok/Clean; with an active call it returns quiet, so the server is still heard). The 2nd signal (cut) is the served attempt's cancellation: going() fails TIMEOUT and drained is cut. stderr told under cut. The box is still settled by Launched::drop (kill+wait), with no signal involvement. Handlers only write signal-hook's CLOEXEC self-pipe, and the ledger keeps its one writer. Mutations M1-M5 cover every new test (ruling 9). Tests assert exact variants, dispositions and causes. rpc/tests.rs is held at exactly 2000 and rpc.rs at 797 (<800). Ran here: broker::rpc::tests::hangup 3/3 pass. FINDINGS (all info): (1) The 4 enabled::signals tests and the 2 new windows tests reported ok in 0.01s in this boxed seat because World::new() skips on an unservable host. I could not observe them or re-run M1-M5 here; the evidence's run-2 record and the controller's host check are their only proof. Exact coverage and macOS CI stay pending as the evidence says. (2) Third-party Claude Code issue reports (not official docs) describe its stdio MCP shutdown as SIGINT, then SIGTERM about 100 ms later, then SIGKILL about 400 ms after that. The fixture spaces signals 1 s apart and bounds closure at <10 s/<5 s, so no test binds the roughly 500 ms a real harness allows before SIGKILL. Under real Claude, an in-flight call will in practice end Failed(timeout) by the SIGTERM rather than by its answer. That is within CR3/CR4 ('existing local ending'), and the answered-call path passed the host check twice. Worth noting for U9b2's guide. (3) Signalled::observed() drops a Signals::new failure via .ok(). It is documented and fails closed: the ledger stays unclosed and CR3 refuses. (4) As the evidence says, repeated same-signal coalescing and the override of an inherited SIG_IGN on SIGINT. A corollary: exec'd children (the server box) now start with SIGINT at SIG_DFL rather than an inherited SIG_IGN. That matters only if a group-wide SIGINT reaches the box, since the server profile sets no --new-session. Not a security finding in my judgement; it is the security member's to weigh. (5) The test-only hangup() helper Box::leaks a closure and flag per call; harmless. Sources: https://claudeissues.com/issue/93087-bug-stdio-mcp-servers-still-connecting-or-queued-at-session-end-are-never-termin ; https://claudeissues.com/issue/31646-mcp-stdio-servers-reported-as-failed-on-exit-despite-clean-shutdown
members.security: Security review of 2fe8308d2..1aff3d020 (U9b1e). Production diff: signal-hook 0.3.18 edge (cfg(unix), lockfile gains only a dependency line, no new crate, no unsafe); Signalled in broker.rs counts SIGINT/SIGTERM from signal-hook's self-pipe under a mutex (handlers write the pipe only; no handler touches the ledger); lifetime.rs folds signal>=1 into startup cancellation (admission/box stage ends with its existing cause) and serving hangs up at >=1, cut (attempt cancellation) at >=2; calls.rs asked() stops reading harness frames once hung up and ends as a closed input only when no call is active. Fail-closed checks: (1) Signals::new failure -> None -> signal kills the process as before, ledger unclosed, CR3 still refuses 'broker ledger lifecycle is invalid' (ledger check unchanged; ledger.rs, adapters.rs, admit.rs untouched). (2) A signal never turns a fatal ending Clean: fatal causes still return Err via going()/heard(); hangup.rs pins a stray answer after hang-up as Protocol. (3) An active call after hang-up is still bounded by its own call deadline, the MB3 untaken bound, and the cut (second signal or orphaning); an unanswered one fails Timeout with a Failed closure (unit + real-binary INT TERM test). (4) Responses after hang-up go through the same masking/retention path; no new journal record, no new error text, nothing signal-derived or model-derived is journaled. (5) Post-Ok drain is bounded by the same attempt cancellation as the existing closed-input path. Info only, not findings: the handlers override an inherited SIG_IGN on SIGINT (and the boxed server child then inherits SIG_DFL, not SIG_IGN, across exec); signal-hook may coalesce two identical signals so a quick double SIGINT counts as one, which still fails closed (deadline or SIGKILL leaves an unclosed ledger that CR3 refuses); any same-uid process (or a box-local server if it could reach the broker's pid) can now end a session Clean by SIGINT, but it could already end it by SIGKILL, and the Clean closure records only honestly-settled calls, so no fabricated outcome or tamper path. Evidence file scanned: no secrets or host paths. No web sources used.

result.notes:
Independently reviewed 2fe8308d2..1aff3d020 against U9b1e/R5/R6, CR3/CR4/MB1 and decisions 0065, 0077 and 0071. The panel's residual/info floor is preserved and raised to low by the chief's finding below. Member verdicts and severity arguments were treated as claims, never directions to this gate.

LOW — chief, decision 0071 ruling 9: openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/evidence/U9b1e.md:99-100 misdescribes M1. Signals::new(ENDING).ok().filter(|_| false) installs handlers, then drops their registrations; signal-hook-registry does not restore the previous/default handlers. An isolated compiled probe against this tree's dependency returned -15 for an unregistered SIGTERM control, but exited 0 and printed 'survived SIGTERM' with the recorded M1 expression. Therefore 'no handler is installed' and 'SIGTERM killed the broker' are incorrect; the fixture's later SIGKILL can explain the unclosed ledger. Correct the recorded mechanism and distinguish dropping registrations from never installing them. The mutation can still bind the signal-handling behaviour; this finding does not invalidate the controller's host check.

INFO — correctness, ruling 9: three in-process hangup tests passed again here. Four enabled::signals tests and two windows::a_signal_at_ tests explicitly skipped because this boxed seat cannot prepare a server box; their reported ok results are not fresh execution proof. M1-M5 full integration reruns remain implementation evidence, not chief-observed runs. Exact coverage outside the box and macOS CI remain pending. Read the controller's host-check-e31bf8ec2-2026-11-01.md and confirmed git diff e31bf8ec2 HEAD -- crates/ Cargo.lock is empty.

INFO — correctness, ruling 9: enabled.rs spaces signals one second apart; signals.rs checks closure within ten/five seconds. These tests do not establish a subsecond harness teardown bound. The panel's external Claude timing claims were not independently verified and are not relied on; no web capability was used.

INFO — correctness/security: broker.rs discards Signals::new errors with .ok(), so successful graceful signal handling is not assured on setup failure. The unchanged ledger validator still refuses missing Closed; neither setup failure nor a signal authorizes a fabricated successful call. Do not generalize the panel's claim that registration removal necessarily restores default termination behaviour, as M1 demonstrates.

INFO — correctness/security: pending signals may coalesce; repeated identical signals need not count twice. Installing SIGINT handling overrides inherited SIG_IGN, and exec children can consequently receive SIG_DFL. These documented lifecycle limits remain; existing deadlines, fatal outcomes and CR3 settlement checks are intact. No weakening of a refusal was found.
